Fix: walk the real static import graph of server.js + Server/run.js (plus the one dynamic import of MtimeFilter.js, which server.js loads by a computed path) fresh on every change, and only restart for a file in that graph. decision.alternative: Could have hand-maintained an allowlist of plugin files instead of walking imports, but that list silently rots the next time someone adds a plugin import line -- the brief explicitly asks for walking the graph for exactly this reason.

decision.what: Build 2 (the page holds): read Socket.js top to bottom. reconnect() already never reloads -- it only sets a backoff retry; reload() is only ever called from changed()/mark_stale paths, never from the socket lifecycle. So the 'blanks on disconnect' bug named in the brief's background does not exist in the code as written today (confirmed it is also not what caused the 15:32 incident, logged above). What was missing: no visible sign at all that a reconnect is in flight -- the owner sees nothing, which is why a restart reads as 'the page died' even though it was already going to come back on its own. Adding show_reconnecting()/hide_reconnecting(): a small fixed strip shown the moment reconnect() schedules its first retry, removed the moment open() succeeds. It is purely cosmetic -- it never reloads, never blocks, never touches $BLOCKRELOAD.
decision.alternative: Could reuse mark_stale's pill, but that pill means 'click to reload' and auto-clearing it on an unrelated event (socket open) would be confusing if a real stale-reload was also pending; a separate, non-clickable strip keeps the two meanings apart.
